second_story.question: Given the contract, context, tools, and authority, why did the failed candidates look correct to their workers?
second_story.answer: The early worker prompts validated the reported counterexample and broad set/count properties but did not begin with a bidirectional semantic matrix derived from text_match's marker contract. Each candidate therefore satisfied the currently visible oracle while dropping another relation: marker preservation, insertion-versus-replacement, or the new-line side relative to preserved survivors. The final prompt made that missing relation executable before implementation and the orchestrator added an independent exhaustive oracle plus a real-model differential.

timeline: ATT-001 replaced sets with occurrence checks but stripped marker semantics and was rejected by four independent counterexamples.
ATT-002 synthesized one expected output and fixed those cases, but forced before-marker insertions to consume preserved originals; independent deterministic_edit parity rejected it.
ATT-003 switched to invariant validation and restored preservation/insertion parity, but allowed new lines to cross marker-preserved survivors; three independent wrong-side cases rejected it.
The automatic depth gate stopped the run; DEC-001 recorded the user's authorization for one additional Claude Opus round.
ATT-004 added occurrence-aware marker-side ordering, passed focused/full/differential/exhaustive checks, and was integrated.
Post-integration validation used the cached FastEdit 1.7B MLX model: the same perfect output scored 0.0 under legacy logic and 1.0 under the integrated validator.
failure_review.impact: No rejected candidate reached the task branch product code. The cost was three extra recovery rounds and delayed integration; user data and external systems were unaffected.
failure_review.expected: One general validator should accept faithful replacement/insertion outcomes while rejecting unsupported deletion, insertion, duplication, reordering, marker leakage, and wrong-side marker placement.
failure_review.observed: Each of the first three candidates closed the preceding hole but omitted another marker relationship that its test matrix did not encode.
contributing_factors: The initial regression matrix was organized by corruption category, not by the full marker-position semantic cross-product.
The W-002 prompt suggested an exact-output synthesizer even though marker fallback can admit multiple locally valid outcomes.
Faithful deterministic_edit parity proved acceptance but did not prove rejection of lines moved across the marker-covered gap.
Worker prompt report-schema summaries omitted several canonical v4.1 identity and structured-row requirements, producing malformed but non-authoritative reports.
failure_review.containment_recovery: All workers edited one isolated Orca worktree. The orchestrator independently rejected each faulty candidate, committed reports unchanged, stopped at the depth gate, obtained DEC-001, added missing negative oracles, validated the final net diff, and only then cherry-picked the worker commits.
failure_review.orchestrator_artifact_change: worker-prompts/W-004.json made before-marker/after-marker side ordering, repeated-occurrence handling, mutation evidence, and the three corrupt outputs mandatory. validation/TASK.json now records exhaustive and real-model differential checks in addition to worker tests.
follow_ups: Future validator prompts should copy the full canonical worker-report v4.1 schema instead of a shortened field-type summary.
When deterministic semantics are the reference, require both positive parity and negative relation-breaking variants for every marker position.
Keep the cached-model tokenizer regex advisory separate from this validator patch; investigate only in a dedicated model-runtime task.

knowledge_added.finding: Marker preservation must be validated as a relation among declared new occurrences, surviving original occurrences, and marker side—not as sets, counts, or one mandatory output.
A faithful-output parity suite needs paired negative transforms; otherwise it proves recall without proving corruption rejection.
Real local-model differential evidence distinguishes validator correctness from assumptions about what the model emits.

new_enforcement.rule: occurrence-aware marker semantic regression matrix with wrong-side mutations

debt_added.principal: Copy the complete canonical v4.1 worker-report grammar into future prompts or validate it before dispatch.

calibration_samples.lesson: Worker success is not validation; semantic counterexamples must be independently generated.
